---

## Goal

Update the game from actions and expose the same state to both renderers.

## Files

- `gridworld/engine.py`

## Tasks

- Complete `Engine(level, controller, renderer)` and its public methods using the supplied interfaces.
- Create the player at the start and handle movement, collisions, waiting, turns and victory.
- Delegate action input to the controller and rendering to the renderer.
- Build independent `JsonState` snapshots and implement the game loop. Integration uses the models from S0-02 and the components from S0-04, assembled by the launcher in S0-05.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The initial state matches `initial_state.json`, including all eight keys, `status="playing"`, turn `0` and an empty message.
- [ ] While playing, each attempted move, including a blocked move, and each `wait` consumes one turn. `None` changes nothing.
- [ ] An action outside the supported vocabulary raises `ValueError` before any mutation.
- [ ] Reaching the exit sets `status="won"` and the exact message `Victory!`.
- [ ] After victory, movement and waiting leave the state unchanged; the loop keeps reading input until `quit`.
- [ ] `quit` stops the loop without changing the game state or consuming a turn.
- [ ] `get_state()` returns a JSON-serializable, independent dictionary without advancing the game; `interaction` remains `None` and `extras` is empty for the base game.
- [ ] `get_action()` calls the controller once. `render(state)` passes the supplied state to `renderer.update_render` once.
- [ ] `run()` renders the initial state and keeps polling input when no action is available. Renderer startup and cleanup belong to the application entry point.

## Evidence

Record these manual scenarios in a reviewed PR linked to this issue, then demonstrate them to the tutor at the start of S1:

1. At the start, `west` leaves the player at `(1, 1)` and advances the turn to `1`. An unknown key changes nothing.
2. In a fresh game, `east, south, south, east, east, east, north, north` reaches `(5, 1)` at turn `8`, with `won` and `Victory!`.
3. After victory, movement and waiting have no effect; `quit` exits cleanly.

Use manual checks in S0. Automated tests begin in S1.
Organize the work and peer reviews within your group.
